app.title: DeepMiRT: miRNA Target Prediction with RNA Foundation Models
app.summary: A person pastes a short regulatory RNA sequence and a candidate target-site sequence, or picks one of the preloaded example pairs. They press Predict and get an interaction probability with a call above or below a fixed threshold, plus a details panel. For many pairs, they upload a CSV with one pair per row, run batch prediction, check a preview of the first rows, and download the table with a probability and a 0/1 call added to every row.

task.text: Score how likely a short RNA is to bind a candidate target site, one pair at a time or a whole table of pairs, using a trained deep-learning model.

data.text: Pairs of nucleotide sequences, a short regulatory RNA and a fixed-length target fragment, typed in one pair at a time or uploaded as a CSV table of pairs
data.item: a pair of a miRNA sequence and a target-site sequence

stage.text: predicting candidate miRNA target sites, before experimental validation

mechanism.text: Two tabs share one model. In the single-pair tab, a two-field form or an example row feeds a large probability readout with a JSON details panel. In the batch tab, an uploaded CSV is scored in batches and comes back as a downloadable file with a preview table.

field.text: deep-learning miRNA target prediction in bioinformatics

workflow.name: score items with a trained model and export the scores

steps.here: Paste a miRNA (15–30 nt) and a target sequence (20–50 nt) in DNA or RNA letters, or click one of the preloaded example pairs

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Predict checks the length and alphabet, converts T to U and runs the model to get an interaction probability

steps.step: identify which items have a property
steps.here: The probability is shown large and coloured, with INTERACTION or NO INTERACTION at a fixed 0.5 threshold, and the sequence lengths in a details panel
Upload a CSV whose column names contain 'mirna' and 'target'. Every row is checked for invalid bases

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Run Batch Prediction scores the rows in batches of 128 and adds a probability column and a 0/1 prediction column
A preview shows the first 20 rows, and the full table can be downloaded as a predictions CSV

distinctive: Inputs are checked against a fixed nucleotide alphabet and length limits, and DNA notation (T) is converted to RNA (U) automatically
The binary call uses a fixed 0.5 probability threshold, shown next to the score
Batch columns are found by matching substrings in the column names, not exact headers
An about tab sets out the model architecture and benchmark standing, so the user knows what the score is based on
